attempts.sql: WITH sql_database AS (SELECT symbol_id FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile WHERE file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py' AND name = 'SQLDatabase' AND is_class = TRUE), sql_database_methods AS (SELECT name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile WHERE enclosing_class_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) AND is_method = TRUE) SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.class_bases AS cb JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS cls ON cls.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS m ON m.enclosing_class_symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id WHERE cb.base_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) AND cls.is_class = TRUE AND cls.in_test_file = FALSE AND m.is_method = TRUE AND m.is_public = TRUE AND m.in_test_file = FALSE AND substr(m.name, 1, 1) <> '_' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sql_database_methods AS sm WHERE sm.name = m.name) ORDER BY cb.class_symbol_id, m.name

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
Return exactly the requested output columns, using each requested name as the column alias, in the requested order. Return complete repository-relative file paths and complete symbol IDs exactly as stored. When the question asks which files, symbols or modules, return each distinct one once unless it asks for occurrences.
explanation: This identifies public methods that are defined directly in production connector classes which list SQLDatabase as a direct base, excluding classes and methods that occur in test files. It joins class base records to the symbol profile so methods are matched to their defining class, then removes any method name that SQLDatabase also defines. Each distinct class-symbol/method-name pair is returned, ordered by class symbol ID and method name.
sql: WITH sql_database AS (SELECT symbol_id FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile WHERE file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py' AND name = 'SQLDatabase' AND is_class = TRUE), sql_database_methods AS (SELECT name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile WHERE enclosing_class_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) AND is_method = TRUE) SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name FROM auto_ontology_code.code.class_bases AS cb JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS cls ON cls.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbol_profile AS m ON m.enclosing_class_symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id WHERE cb.base_symbol_id IN (SELECT symbol_id FROM sql_database) AND cls.is_class = TRUE AND cls.in_test_file = FALSE AND m.is_method = TRUE AND m.is_public = TRUE AND m.in_test_file = FALSE AND substr(m.name, 1, 1) <> '_' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sql_database_methods AS sm WHERE sm.name = m.name) ORDER BY cb.class_symbol_id, m.name
